claims.text: The bulk (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits a large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
The unmodified alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and is susceptible to cracking under cyclic operation.
A CoCrFeNi-based coating is sufficiently ductile to protect the substrate.
An approximately 1 μm CoCrFeNi-based film can be deposited at room temperature by the proposed magnetron-sputtering route.
An intermediate graded layer will improve adhesion and mitigate thermal-expansion mismatch.
A post-deposition anneal at 400–500 °C in an inert atmosphere is suitable for the coated alloy.
The proposed processing will produce a well-adhered nanocrystalline coating.
The coating and graded layer will establish a beneficial compressive residual-stress profile.
The coating process will reinforce the near-surface region without altering the bulk crystallography.
The ductile coating will redistribute mechanical stresses.
The coating will blunt or suppress surface crack initiation.
Limiting the coating thickness to approximately 1 μm will prevent interference with the bulk phase transformation responsible for the caloric effect.
The coated alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the uncoated alloy.
The coated alloy will have improved load-bearing capacity and resistance to crack propagation.
The coating will preserve the magnitude of the unmodified alloy's caloric response to within the proposed 10% criterion.
The coating will preserve the temperature range of the unmodified alloy's caloric effect.
The intervention will remain effective under magnetic fields up to 3–5 T.
The intervention will remain effective under pressure fields up to several hundred MPa.
The intervention will remain effective from room temperature to approximately 50 °C.
The coating interface will withstand cyclic magnetic, pressure, and thermal loading without significant degradation or delamination.
